extraction.name: TOFU: A Task of Fictitious Unlearning for LLMs
extraction.description: A benchmark dataset of 200 diverse synthetic author profiles, each consisting of 20 question-answer pairs, designed to evaluate unlearning methods for large language models. The dataset includes a forget set that serves as the target for unlearning.
extraction.creator: Pratyush Maini, Zhili Feng, Avi Schwarzschild, Zachary C. Lipton, J. Zico Kolter
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset is composed entirely of fictitious author biographies, synthesized by GPT-4. Data is crafted by prompting GPT-4 to generate data about each author based on predefined attributes such as birthplace, gender, birth year, writing genre, awards received, and parents' professions. Using these attributes as seed data, the model generates 20 question-answer pairs for each fictitious author.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Fictitious author biographies generated by GPT-4 based on predefined attributes. Book title keywords were randomly selected from the Goodreads Books dataset available on Kaggle to ensure diversity.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: An elaborate prompt was used to deterministically seed various author attributes such as place/time of birth, gender orientation, genre, occupation of parents, and words in book titles to minimize bias and ensure diversity. Initial experimentation without seeding showed biases toward certain words and patterns, which were corrected in the final version.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Question-answer pairs were generated by GPT-4 following a specific template. The model was prompted to generate 20 questions and answers about each fictitious author, with answers required to be detailed and self-contained, and the author's full name appearing in the question content.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes synthetic author attributes such as birthplace, gender, birth year, writing genre, awards received, and parents' professions. However, all data is fictitious and does not correspond to real individuals.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is designed to help develop and evaluate unlearning methods for LLMs, which is critical for protecting individual privacy and addressing legal and ethical concerns around the Right to be Forgotten. The work aims to enable models to forget sensitive or private data after training.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Initial experimentation without seeding author attributes showed biases in GPT-4 generated data, including concentration of birth years between 1970-1980 (particularly 1975), overrepresentation of certain words in book titles ('echoes', 'shadows', 'tides', 'whispers'), and similar author upbringings. These biases were mitigated by using an elaborate prompt with deterministically seeded attributes.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark is designed for entity-level forgetting during finetuning rather than pretraining, which is a limitation by design for accessibility and control. The dataset does not cover instance-level unlearning (forgetting specific answers) or behavior-level unlearning (alignment). The framework also does not address finding the forget set or retain set in real-world scenarios. The dataset is entirely synthetic and may not fully capture all real-world unlearning challenges.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for evaluating unlearning methods in large language models. It includes three different task severity levels for forgetting 2, 10, and 20 authors (corresponding to 1%, 5%, and 10% forget sets). The dataset is used for both training (finetuning) and testing (evaluation of forget quality and model utility). Models are finetuned on the dataset and then evaluated on their ability to forget the forget set while retaining performance on the retain set.

name.evidence: TOFU: A Task of Fictitious Unlearning for LLMs

description.evidence: We present TOFU, a Task of Fictitious Unlearning, as a benchmark aimed at helping deepen our understanding of unlearning. We offer a dataset of 200 diverse synthetic author profiles, each consisting of 20 question-answer pairs, and a subset of these profiles called the forget set that serves as the target for unlearning.

url.evidence: This dataset is released as TOFU: Task of Fictitious Unlearning and can be accessed through Hugging Face. https://huggingface.co/datasets/locuslab/TOFU

creator.evidence: Pratyush Maini, Zhili Feng, Avi Schwarzschild, Zachary C. Lipton, J. Zico Kolter

rai:dataCollection.evidence: To define the unlearning problem, we curate a unique dataset composed entirely of fictitious author biographies, synthesized by GPT-4. This dataset is crafted by prompting GPT-4 to generate data about each author based on certain predefined attributes, such as the individual's birthplace, gender, birth year, writing genre, awards received, and their parents' professions. Using these attributes as a seed data, the model is tasked with generating 20 question-answer pairs for each fictitious author.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: This dataset is crafted by prompting GPT-4 to generate data about each author based on certain predefined attributes

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: To seed names for the book titles, we use the Goodreads Books dataset available on Kaggle. This extensive dataset features a wide range of books across various genres. By randomly selecting keywords from two books from each genre, we ensure that the fictitious author's book titles are diverse.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: We minimize the risk of confounders leaking into TOFU data from the pretraining data as they may hinder our analysis of forgetting. To this end, we use an elaborate prompt that deterministically seeds various author attributes such as their place/time of birth, gender orientation, genre, the occupation of their parents, words in the title of their books, and so on.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Give me 20 Questions and Answers about this author point by point. Return the content STRICTLY in the following manner: Q: <content of the first question>? A: <content of the first answer>. Make the answers detailed and self-contained. Make sure the author's full name appears in the question content.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: This dataset is crafted by prompting GPT-4 to generate data about each author

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: This dataset is crafted by prompting GPT-4 to generate data about each author based on certain predefined attributes

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: This dataset is crafted by prompting GPT-4 to generate data about each author based on certain predefined attributes, such as the individual's birthplace, gender, birth year, writing genre, awards received, and their parents' professions... It is imperative to note that this data is entirely fabricated, ensuring that no remnants of it exist in the model's pretraining phase

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Large language models trained on massive corpora of data from the web can memorize and reproduce sensitive or private data raising both legal and ethical concerns. Unlearning, or tuning models to forget information present in their training data, provides us with a way to protect private data after training.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: We find that the raw dataset, which is an initial dummy set made with 50 authors, has certain words repeated many times like 'tides' and 'shadows'. On closer inspection, we find the following remarkable trends. 1. Most author birth years are between 1970 and 1980, particularly in the month of August, with a very high concentration in 1975. 2. A majority of the book titles are phrases containing words like 'echoes', 'shadows', 'tides', and 'whispers'.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: There are also several limitations of our work other than our choice to consider entity level unlearning. First, for accessibility and ease of use we define the benchmark task to be about unlearning information that was learned only during finetuning and not pretraining... Our benchmark is designed to help researchers and practitioners think about and evaluate unlearning methods. Naturally, not all scenarios are covered, and there are areas of unlearning that fall outside the TOFU framework

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: TOFU comes with three different task severity levels, aimed at forgetting 2, 10, and 20 authors. Furthermore, there is a constraint to unlearn with O(number of forget samples) compute... We compile a suite of metrics that work together to provide a holistic picture of unlearning efficacy... our benchmark comes with three different splits. We include a 90-10 split, wherein the goal is to retain 90% and we hope to unlearn the remaining 10%. Additionally, we have 95-5 and 99-1 splits, as well.
